text:
jordan_cs: Hello team, Hummingbird onboarding: they report 5-10s windows of 429s immediately after users sign up and hit the welcome flow. Its causing failed welcome messages.

devin_eng: Likely SDK preflight or telemetry batching. Any sample headers?

tabitha_support: They shared one: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-ratelimit: 100;window=60
x-rw-reset: 18
Body: {"error":"rate_limit","msg":"preflight overload"}
```
Theyre using our Node SDK server-side but they also have a client-side web hook that pings our endpoint during sign-up to prewarm embeddings cache.

sam_se: If server and client both call during sign-up, you can get short-lived bursts. Recommend: (1) serialize sign-up related API calls server-side, (2) prewarm embeddings with lower-priority background job, (3) check request IDs to de-duplicate.

devin_eng: For immediate fix, instruct client to use our `defer:true` option on the SDK so preflight is deferred until after UI renders. Eg: `new RWSDK({defer:true})`. That reduces immediate handshake pressure.

jordan_cs: Hummingbird turned on `defer:true` and also queued their embed prewarm to run 30s after sign-up. They reported the 429s dropped to zero in the following hour.

ratebot: rate-limiter: spike window at 3123469020 - peak 35 reqs/s - tags: signup-flow

tabitha_support: I'll add a playbook note: "If 429s around signup, consider deferring SDK init or moving heavy prewarm tasks to background with jitter."

sam_se: Also recommending they adopt our server-side batching util for embeddings to collapse small repeated requests.

jordan_cs: Great. I'll update the onboarding checklist and mark Hummingbird as green. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
